Claim (technical, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The hard fork would introduce new Plutus primitives for modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 multi-scalar multiplication, arrays, and native Value handling, with linked CIP references for each primitive set.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal says all Plutus built-in functions will become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3, expanding capabilities for existing V1 and V2 scripts.
Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposal says native case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data in UPLC will improve performance and produce cleaner script logic.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposal says testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete specification-to-implementation conformance for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus features across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.

Claim (technical, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The proposal links a Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report and says it shows no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks, plus acceptable baseline performance for new Plutus primitives and case expressions.
